text:
Maya: Quick idea — can we standardize a short postmortem follow-up cadence? I'm seeing action items slip and owners unclear after handoff.
Sam: +1. I keep losing track of which remediations are in the 14-day window vs longer term.
Kevin: Agree. Proposal: 3 checkpoints — 48h triage, 14-day remediation check, 90-day recurrence review.
Elena: That sounds reasonable. Can we make the 14-day check a required calendar invite from the incident owner?
Maya: Yeah — owner creates a 30-min 'PM follow-up' invite within 72h of closure, add eng-oncall and SRE.
Nate: Also let's add a simple template for the 14-day check so it's quick to run.
Maya: I sketched one:
```
14-day follow-up template:
- Owner: <name>
- Remediation items: (list with links to tickets)
- Status: on-track / blocked / deferred
- ETA changes: yes/no + new ETA
- Risk: regression probability (low/med/high)
- Actions this meeting: assign owners + deadlines
- Follow-up needed: yes/no -> schedule next check
```
Sam: Nice. Can we also tag actions with an SLA-like expectation? e.g., P1 remediations due in 7 days, P2 in 30?
Kevin: Let's be pragmatic: critical safety fixes = 7d, major reliability = 30d, everything else 90d. Owners can request extensions with a short justification.
Elena: For ownership clarity, add a single point-of-contact field on the postmortem doc. That person is responsible for creating the follow-up invite and updating tickets.
Maya: Agreed. Also suggest we keep a lightweight public tracker: a table in the incident doc's top, and a centralized weekly digest posted to #eng-oncall for anything older than 14 days.
Nate: Mechanically, IncidentBot could post a digest. Pete (SRE) built a small script we can reuse.
IncidentBot: Automated reminder: "2039203456 follow-up due" scheduled — assigned to Maya.
Sam: On comms cadence — propose: closure announcement -> 48h triage summary -> 14-day owner update -> 90-day recurrence note. All short, single-paragraph messages.
Kevin: Also rotate incident commander (IC) nominations monthly. We should keep a simple IC roster doc and a one-line runbook for handoffs.
Elena: How about a 1-hour monthly IC sync to cover ongoing remediations across incidents? Could reduce duplicate work.
Maya: Good call. I'll draft a short runbook and a calendar for the first rotation, plus the 14-day template.
Nate: I'll wire IncidentBot to post the 14-day reminders to owners and create the weekly digest skeleton.
Sam: Can we add a lightweight tagging convention on tickets, e.g., incident-<id>:remediation and remediation-owner:<githubhandle>? That will help queries.
Kevin: Yes — and add a default board view filtered to "open remediations" for oncall review.
Elena: One more: recurrence signals — add a quick checklist at 90-day: frequency increase, similar root cause in last 12 months, outstanding mitigations.
Maya: We'll try this for the next 2 months and review adoption. If owners miss the 14-day check twice, escalate to team lead.
Sam: Sounds fair. Anything else?
Kevin: Request: can we make the 14-day check an optional column in the postmortem template so it's visible in the table view?
Maya: Yep — I'll include it. Drafting now and will @mention folks when done. :rocket:
Nate: I'll push the IncidentBot changes to staging tomorrow.
IncidentBot: Follow-up created: "2039203456 - 14-day check" assigned to Maya, reminder in 14 days.
Maya: Thanks everyone — will share the draft and a one-page IC rotation doc by EOD Friday.
